item.title: Draft fisheries ordinances and new notice on foreign-operated recreational fishing vessels
item.description: AI summary: The proposed Ministerial Ordinance would amend implementing rules on foreign fishing and fishing in Japan's exclusive economic zone, clarifying the scope of minor harvesting using vessels of at least three gross tons, including recreational fishing vessels owned by foreign-managed Japanese corporations and foreign sole proprietors. It would also expressly allow qualifying permanent residents and other persons excluded from the statutory definition of foreigners to supervise such harvesting, reorganize gear categories, and include harvesting by bare hands. The excerpts state that the proposed vessel treatment would not change the definition of a Japanese vessel under the Ship Act. A proposed new Notice would designate vessels under Article 2(7) of the Act on Regulation of Fishing Operations by Foreign Nationals, but the supplied excerpts do not establish its precise designation criteria. The Fisheries Agency published the proposals for public comment on 2026-11-13; the stated deadline was 2026-12-12 23:59 JST. Original title: 外国人漁業の規制に関する法律施行規則及び排他的経済水域における漁業等に関する主権的権利の行使等に関する法律施行規則の一部改正案及び外国人漁業の規制に関する法律第2条第7項の農林水産大臣の指定する船舶を定める件の制定案についての意見・情報の募集について Public Comment Open | e-Gov Public Comment | Published 2026-11-13 | First detected 2026-11-13 Monitoring aid only; not legal advice or an official translation. item.title: Digital Fisheries Strategy Hub: Uku-Ojika Selected in Second FY2026 Round
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-09, the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries announced the selection of the Uku-Ojika area in Nagasaki Prefecture as a new Digital Fisheries Strategy Hub in the second selection round for fiscal 2026. The regional plan under consideration covers automatic fishing-vessel track collection to improve operations, combining track and catch data for stock assessments, data sharing with restaurant and processing businesses, and satellite positioning and communications for vessel safety. It envisages using the "Triton's Spear" track-data system and "Triton's Spear Rescue" safety system, with the aim of building a model linking fishing, resource assessment and sales that could be replicated elsewhere. This is a project-selection announcement, not a stated change to legal obligations. item.title: MAFF certifies smart-agriculture development and supply plans
item.description: AI summary: On 2026-11-06, the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries announced two new plan certifications under the Act on Promotion of the Use of Smart Agriculture Technologies to Improve Agricultural Productivity (Act No. 63 of 2024), plus certification of a change to Kubota Corporation's plan originally certified in May 2025. The new plans were reviewed under Article 13(4), and Kubota's change under Article 14(1) and Article 13(4) as applied through Article 14(6); certified operators can receive financial, tax and other support. REACT Corporation's five-year plan covers development and supply of an autonomous air-blown pollination system for greenhouse strawberries, described as contributing to a 30% increase in added value. Hatakehotoke Corporation's three-year plan covers development and supply of an autonomous weeding device for organic rice cultivation using the Michibiki quasi-zenith satellite system and soil-agitating brushes, described as contributing to an 80% reduction in weeding labor time. These are plan certifications under an existing Act, not amendments to legislation. Original title: 「農業の生産性の向上のためのスマート農業技術の活用の促進に関する法律」に基づき開発供給実施計画を認定しました Government Announcement | Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF) | Published 2026-11-06 | First detected 2026-11-07 Monitoring aid only; not legal advice or an official translation.
